verdict.rationale: RustDesk documents a free OSS ID/rendezvous server (hbbs) and relay server (hbbr) that you deploy on your own infrastructure, with a Docker compose setup. Clients connect peer to peer when possible and otherwise fall back to your relay. Several users report running their own lookup/relay servers successfully for years. missing for 10: built-in authentication on the OSS self-hosted server (users report it is open to anyone unless placed behind a VPN; Pro adds auth), and consistent hands-on reports of easy setup (some users found self-hosting difficult).

support.subject: As an IT admin, I can self-host the rendezvous or relay infrastructure so session traffic stays on infrastructure I run

citations.quote: Server OSS: a free, open-source ID/rendezvous server (hbbs) and relay server (hbbr) that you can deploy on your own infrastructure.
Self-hosted ID/rendezvous and relay servers with Server OSS or Server Pro; clients connect peer to peer when they can and fall back to your relay.
You can use our rendezvous/relay server, set up your own, or write your own rendezvous/relay server.
Has used it for years with their own lookup/relay server and says it keeps getting better.
